utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we look at 1D1207, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the 1st Motorised Brigade was positioned opposite from Grbavica and that the HVO was opposite Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: KDZ310
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the Muslim side, it was the area of responsibility of the 1st Muslim Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: KDZ310
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were not aware of who was in front of you?

utterances.speaker: KDZ310
utterances.text: As far as we were concerned, it was the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Muslims, however you want to call them, but I'm not -- I didn't know the name of the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we look at this document. This is an executive order for assault actions in the region of Grbavica, dated the 2nd of January, 1993, the second day of the new year; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ310
utterances.text: What are you asking what is correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you if you knew that an order was issued for an attack on Grbavica then.

utterances.speaker: KDZ310
utterances.text: I don't know, Mr. Karadzic. I was living in Grbavica, not in Marin Dvor. I wasn't living with Zlatko Lagumdzija. How can I know that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. But he's issuing an order for an attack to be carried out in the Grbavica sector. Can we look at page 2 --

utterances.speaker: KDZ310
utterances.text: What do you mean, that when he issues an order he's going to inform me about it so that I would know? How could I know that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was there an attack on Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: KDZ310
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at the paragraph titled "Task." "Occupy region to the right, Transit; to the left-most, by the Elektroprivreda. Attack to be executed through the direction of 11 Blue, south side of the Grbavica Stadium, palm, shopping and Strojorad, four big skyscrapers, with the goal to break the enemy on the given locations and to occupy important buildings."

utterances.speaker: KDZ310
utterances.text: The locations are familiar.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at page 4 now, please; page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you look at the bottom: "Since the capture of a fortified settlement like this, it's impossible to do this without destruction and torching of buildings, which are at the same time strong enforcements, destroy and torch everything so that the operation could be carried out safely in order -- due to the familiar insolence, lack of principles, do not believe a single captured soldier, especially those who have any kind of weapons with them."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Karadzic repeat the last sentence of his question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, the interpreters didn't hear your last part of your question. Could you repeat it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to ask the witness -- and then after that I'm going to ask for a minute in closed session. I wanted to ask him this:

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see what the intentions are of your enemies at the time; to destroy and torch everything, to -- not to trust those captured, especially if they had weapons, so meaning they could be captured without weapons? What do you understand this "do not trust anyone captured" to mean?

utterances.speaker: KDZ310
utterances.text: I don't know what they wanted to say with that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we move into private session for a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karadzic. Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, Mr. Karadzic spoke to you about the expulsion that you have testified about, and he basically put into doubt what you were telling, and also said that would that have happened, it would have been widely known and broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In this context, I would like to have Exhibit -- 65 ter 45135 be played. And as it is being played, just to say what it is: It is a report from TV Belgrade about a press conference of UNPROFOR, deputy head of mission in Belgrade, and we will see. I hope it works. We play just a very short sequence.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We would need the translation, the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note that this is very, very fast. We would need a transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We don't have a transcript, but it is only about the first -- really, very first sentences that are spoken. And if we repeat it, it should actually be clear, what this is about. Can we perhaps -- it's just a few seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So can we hear it again or can we start from the beginning again?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may ask my learned friend, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, to let us know the date of the event, the date of the press conference, because if somebody went under fire, as it says here, as the announcer says, then they were exposed to firing. Then we have to see when the authority was set up or before that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you give us the date, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I cannot give you the exact date, but it is -- as it becomes clear from the narrative, that it is a complaint done by General Morillon, and it's -- and his time-period was September 1992 to July 1993. I would not exactly know what he's talking about, but I was actually thinking that the witness can help us with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "There was ethnic cleansing in Grbavica yesterday, when about 300 people were expelled to the Hotel Bristol under fire, about which General Morillon protested to Radovan Karadzic."

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: That is -- that is sufficient. Thank you very much that you could do it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, do you know about this event, that 300 people were expelled to Bristol -- Hotel Bristol?

utterances.speaker: KDZ310
utterances.text: I know of it, yes. I'm aware of it. In the direction of the Hotel Bristol, not at the Hotel Bristol, because that was on the firing line. People were expelled over the pedestrian bridge that was next to the Hotel Bristol, so this was in the direction of that hotel.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And would you know what -- approximately when this happened?

utterances.speaker: KDZ310
utterances.text: This was in the summer of 1992. I'm not sure, but I think that's when it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And such reports, here it is the TV Belgrade. Are you aware that such -- did you, yourself, see TV Belgrade, and would you see such reports?

utterances.speaker: KDZ310
utterances.text: We were able to watch television from Belgrade when we had electricity. So this doesn't happen very often. I really don't remember reports like this from Belgrade Television. I cannot confirm them. We were able to watch Belgrade Television when we had electricity.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to have this clip admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: For the record, could you give us the 65 ter number again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1951, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's still necessary for us to be informed about the time, the date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We heard what Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff said, and --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I also can say that I recall that this was also discussed with -- I think with Witness Doyle or Abdel-Razek. I'm not sure about -- one of the two. And there was actually a protest done by UNPROFOR, and it is an exhibit in this case. I can definitely look for this and provide the information later on, but at the moment I just can't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And if time allows, can we also have another very short clip, and it is 65 ter 40171H, and it's just the minutes 31:12 to 32. And as it is being played: It is TV Sarajevo this time, also referring to expulsion from Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "The MUP of Bosnia and Herzegovina issued an announcement stating that two groups of approximately 500 citizens each crossed over into free territory from Grbavica I and II. According to this information, they were thrown out of their apartments this morning without prior notice. Their keys to their apartments were confiscated, and they were told that they would get an explanation when they crossed to the other side. The MUP informs us that an SDS meeting was held that morning where it was stated that it was --" The interpreters note that this is really very, very fast.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It's actually -- it's sufficient what we've heard so far, and my question to the witness would be:

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you know about this expulsion?

utterances.speaker: KDZ310
utterances.text: I don't know which time-period this covers. I don't remember exactly the date, the month, the year of each of the expulsions. There were several of them. I'm not able to confirm for you when this one took place.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, according to the information that I got, it should have been the 30th of September, 1992. That's what the programme refers to as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you confirm that with the witness? If it is the 30th of September, 1992, do you have anything to say about that expulsion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I said, I do not know the date, so I cannot confirm that two groups of 500 citizens from Grbavica were expelled on what day. I know that the expulsions did take place, that groups of citizens were expelled, but I don't remember the dates.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to object. This is propaganda by the Muslim television, and at that time it was not possible to carry out exchanges without the permission of these officers that were dealing with population exchanges.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was not an exchange of population. These were expulsions. When there were expulsions from the other side, there were no Serbs coming.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's not helpful. It is not for you, Mr. Karadzic, to intervene at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, and if I understand the information correctly, the date is actually mentioned in the news. This is what I think, but I didn't hear it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But the witness said he cannot confirm about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Then let me ask you this: What you saw mentioned here, is that what you, yourself, saw reflected on the ground?

utterances.speaker: KDZ310
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask permission -- admission of this document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could we confirm with the interpreters whether the date was mentioned? Could we hear it again?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "We received an announcement from the MUP of Bosnia and Herzegovina that today, two groups of 500 citizens each crossed into free territory. They were expelled from their apartments without prior notice. There were -- keys and other property were confiscated from them, and they were told that they would be given information when they cross over. There was also information that the SDS held a meeting, stating that all Croats and Muslims would need to be expelled from that area."

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's -- I can't clarify the date right now. Perhaps it's possible to clarify that later.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note that the only reference to the date was the word "danas," "today." There was no date.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Allow me to say that this policeman should be called to testify so that he can say that some Seselj or Arkan's men were in Grbavica. There were no such people at Grbavica. This was something that could not have been done without the commissions. Perhaps this document can be admitted once we have the testimony of the policeman who mentioned that there were Seselj's and Arkan's men in Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you will consider that option, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, tendering this document later on?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would actually suggest that we mark this for identification, and I will provide the additional information about when this TV programme was broadcast during the next sessions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Albeit in response to a leading question, the witness confirmed that what he saw is reflected in this video. On that basis, we'll mark this for identification, pending the clarification from the OTP as to its date.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And no more questions. I'm finished.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be MFI P1952.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, that concludes your evidence. Thank you for your coming to the Tribunal to give it. You are now free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you wait a minute so that you can go. I take it the next hearing date will be 7th of December. We'll resume with Mr. Konings' evidence?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The hearing is now adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 7th day of December, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.
